title: InterConFuzz: A Fuzzing-based Comprehensive NoC Verification Framework
problem: Security verification of Network-on-Chip (NoC) systems is challenging due to intricate high-concurrency structures; traditional verification methods fail to achieve comprehensive coverage, leading to prolonged verification and overlooked security vulnerabilities.
motivation: NoCs are critical infrastructure in SoCs but remain under-verified for security; comprehensive yet efficient verification is essential to catch subtle vulnerabilities before silicon.
method: InterConFuzz works by combining two complementary testing techniques: fuzzing, which systematically generates random inputs to explore system behavior, and symbolic execution, which analyzes all possible code paths those inputs could take through the system. The tool is built on UVM (Universal Verification Methodology, the industry-standard framework for hardware testing), allowing it to integrate into existing verification workflows. By applying this hybrid approach to NoC systems (the communication networks inside chips that coordinate many parallel operations), InterConFuzz exhaustively searches for security vulnerabilities in high-concurrency scenarios that traditional verification methods typically miss.
key_novelty: InterConFuzz combines fuzzing and symbolic execution to comprehensively verify the security of Network-on-Chip systems.
contributions: Hybrid fuzzing + symbolic execution for NoC security
Discovery of 5 security flaws in OpenTitan SoC NoC (vs 2 for prior techniques)
24.4% reduction in memory consumption vs. existing approaches

metrics.other: 24.4% memory reduction, 29.5% compute reduction, 5 flaws found vs 2 prior

limitations: Evaluation limited to OpenTitan SoC; applicability to other NoC topologies and verification completeness claims not fully substantiated.
primary_theme: hybrid fuzzing framework for NoC security verification
